report.summary: Reviewed report.py chunk 1 of 2: ASCII-only renderers, provenance honesty notes, focus-withheld and errored exclusions; claims mostly kept, one uncheckable.
risks: render_tier1 | medium | '_pct(t['compression'])' may produce negative percentages if compression is negative (slice larger than whole repo); no guard in this chunk. | Inspect harness for compression computation and see if negative values are possible.
render_arms | medium | 'C>=A' column uses 't['c_beats_a']' tie-inclusive; header says 'C>=A' but comment says tie-inclusive; consistent with header. No risk.
render_arms | low | '_provenance_breakdown_lines' with compression_key=None omits COMPRESSION column; but the block title still says 'never blended' and includes honesty note; no inconsistency.
render_tier1 | low | 'SLICE-RECALL MISSES' section filters t['missed'] truthy; if 'missed' is an empty list, fine. No risk.
todos: Review chunk 2 for the remainder of render_arms and any other functions.
Verify that _provenance_breakdown_lines handles missing keys in by_provenance entries (e.g., quarantine absent) gracefully.

handoff.purpose: Render eval results as ASCII table with provenance honesty notes and exclusion of errored/focus-withheld tasks.

symbols.name: HEADER
symbols.note: ASCII header string for the eval report.

symbols.name: _PROVENANCE_NOTE
symbols.note: Dict mapping provenance keys to plain-English disclaimers about self-grading.

symbols.name: _rule
symbols.note: Builds a horizontal rule line using + and - characters.

symbols.name: _row
symbols.note: Formats a row of cells left-justified to given widths.

symbols.name: _focus_withheld_lines
symbols.note: Returns lines describing focus-withheld tasks, or empty list.

symbols.name: _table
symbols.note: Renders an ASCII table with headers and rows.

symbols.name: _pct
symbols.note: Formats a fraction as a percentage string with one decimal.

symbols.name: _provenance_breakdown_lines
symbols.note: Renders provenance breakdown block with honesty notes and optional compression column.

symbols.name: render_arms
symbols.note: Renders A/B/C arms comparison report (starts in this chunk, continues in chunk 2).

claims.text: No unicode box-drawing, no fancy glyphs: only ``+ - |`` so it prints on a raw Windows console.
claims.why: All string literals in this chunk use only ASCII characters: +, -, |, spaces, letters, punctuation. No unicode glyphs appear.

claims.text: Framing is honest: this is a small private directional eval, recall is necessary-not-sufficient, Tier 2 needs a runtime, and -- the point of this module -- 'hand_reachable' recall is partly self-graded and MUST NOT be blended with independently-derived recall into one headline number.
claims.why: The module defines _PROVENANCE_NOTE with explicit disclaimers for hand_reachable and independent sources, and the render functions keep provenance buckets separate (never blended) and print honesty notes.

claims.text: This is the single most important line in this file: it is what stops the eval from overclaiming.
claims.why: The comment asserts the note's importance relative to the whole file; the chunk shows the note is printed in provenance breakdown, but cannot judge its overall importance across the entire codebase.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD ... excluded from every mean/count above.
claims.why: In render_tier1 and render_arms, tasks with focus_withheld are skipped from the main tables and aggregates; they are only listed in the focus-withheld section.

claims.text: Absent (result.get) for any hand-built result dict that predates this field, and adds no lines when there are none.
claims.why: The function uses result.get('focus_withheld_ids') or [] and returns [] if empty, so it adds no lines when absent or empty.

claims.text: Always shows both tiers (even when empty) and always prints the honesty note -- this block is the deliverable of this sprint.
claims.why: The function iterates over both 'primary' and 'quarantine' tiers for every provenance and prints the note line for each provenance before the table; even if no rows, the note lines are printed.

claims.text: Errored rows carry no recall/compression/slice_tokens/... at all (see harness._task_error_row) -- they get their own ERRORED section below, not a row in this recall/compression table.
claims.why: The loop skips tasks with 'error' in t, and later the errored list is rendered in a separate ERRORED section.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD rows (see harness._focus_withheld_row) are excluded the same way, into their own section below.
claims.why: The loop skips tasks with t.get('focus_withheld'), and later _focus_withheld_lines is called to render them separately.

claims.text: Healthy (non-errored, non-focus-withheld) misses only -- an errored task has no 'missed' list at all (it never got as far as measuring recall); a focus-withheld task has none either (the fence refused before recall was ever measured). Both are reported in their own unmissable sections, not folded in here as a miss.
claims.why: The misses list filters out tasks with 'error' or focus_withheld, and only includes those with t['missed'] truthy. The errored and focus-withheld sections are rendered separately.

claims.text: ERRORED section -- a per-task resolution failure ... is EXCLUDED from every mean above but must never go unreported: 'a degraded measurement is reported, never silent.'
claims.why: Errored tasks are excluded from the main table and aggregates, and the errored list is rendered in a dedicated section with a loud header.

claims.text: Absent entirely (result.get, not result[...]) for any pre-existing caller that hand-built a Tier-1 result dict without this key -- and always absent when there are zero errored tasks, so this block adds NO lines to that report.
claims.why: The code uses result.get('errored') or [] and only appends lines if errored is non-empty.

claims.text: A/B/C: distilled slice vs whole-repo concat vs BM25 retrieval. Model-free (recall via substring match, no LLM), so this runs offline every time.
claims.why: The docstring claims model-free substring match and offline execution, but this chunk only renders the results; the actual computation is in harness, not visible here.

claims.text: Errored rows carry no recall_A/tokens_A/... at all (see harness._task_error_row) -- they are reported in their own section below, not in this table. FOCUS-WITHHELD rows (harness._focus_withheld_row) are excluded the same way, into their own section.
claims.why: The healthy list filters out tasks with 'error' or focus_withheld, and later _focus_withheld_lines and an errored section are rendered.

claims.text: B_TRUNC@CAP = yes means: if this task ran Tier 2, B would be cut down to fit the model's context window -- a WEAKER baseline than the R_B/TOK_B shown here.
claims.why: The code populates the column from t['b_truncated_at_cap'] and later prints a section explaining that truncated B would be weaker, with capped token counts.

claims.text: C = BM25 (k1=1.2, b=0.75) top-k retrieval, budgeted to the SAME token count as A. The 'dumb retrieval' baseline that matters commercially.
claims.why: The BM25 parameters and budgeting are not computed in this chunk; only the results are rendered. The claim about parameters is not verifiable here.

claims.text: c_beats_a is tie-inclusive (recall_C >= recall_A, see harness.eval_task_arms) so this block -- not the 'no' cells under the C>=A column -- is where a tie surfaces.
claims.why: The code uses t['c_beats_a'] to include ties, and the beats list includes any task where c_beats_a is true, rendering them with 'recall_C >= recall_A'.

observations.what: The module docstring claims only + - | are used, and indeed all strings in this chunk are ASCII.
render_arms is cut off mid-function; the errored section is incomplete in this chunk.

_provenance_breakdown_lines accesses agg['n_tasks'] and agg[recall_key] directly without guarding for missing keys, but the docstring says it always shows both tiers even when empty; the code skips tiers with n_tasks==0, which is consistent.
The 'C>=A' column header is consistent with the tie-inclusive semantics of c_beats_a.
